missing_pieces.duty: ED26-METHOD-maximum-entropy-C04 (partial): The inferential interpretation is reconstructed only as far as the Section 2 premises (J1)-(J5) and the application limits (043 lines 398-532). The paper's own stated justificatory claims are missing, so the interpretation is not shown to be conditional on all the premises the paper states. Missing claims: (i) the rules of statistical mechanics are justified as inference independently of physical argument and of experimental verification, and the maximum-entropy estimates remain the best obtainable from the information whatever experiment shows (abstract p. 620; p. 626); (ii) the inferential reading makes the hypotheses of ergodicity, metric transitivity and equal a priori probabilities unnecessary. The paper argues this from three points: the laws of motion add no information beyond measurement; there is no rational basis for excluding any state the information allows, which acts like an ergodic hypothesis whether or not the system is ergodic; and the conclusion section reaches the usual relations without ensembles or ergodic arguments (abstract; p. 621 'reversal'; p. 623; pp. 624-625; p. 627; p. 629); (iii) inventing a fictitious ensemble cannot change the subjective standing of the probabilities (p. 626). None of these appears in 043/044 or anywhere else on the route, yet 043 lines 704-709 present Sections 1-6 as the treated extent. The required extent is the complete inferential argument of the original paper, so the reconstruction is incomplete.

required_components.description: Specify the measurand and measurement equation; distinguish error, correction and uncertainty.
required_components.success_condition: Give an explicit quantity, units, input roles and uncertain corrections.
required_components.failure_condition: Treat uncertainty as an observed error or the standard deviation as every source of uncertainty.

required_components.description: Derive covariance propagation and state the first-order boundary.
required_components.success_condition: Derive u²(y)=JΣJᵀ under its approximation conditions and retain covariance terms.
required_components.failure_condition: Use the independent-input formula for shared calibration errors or declare the Taylor approximation exact.

required_components.description: Separate Type A/Type B evaluations from random/systematic error terminology.
required_components.success_condition: Explain each information source and attach its uncertainty evaluation to the same model.
required_components.failure_condition: Call Type B subjective error without an assigned information model or equate the two classifications.

required_components.description: Explain coverage factors and nonlinear failure.
required_components.success_condition: Show why a quoted coverage factor needs conditions and supply a nonlinear countercase.
required_components.failure_condition: Treat k=2 as universally exact 95% coverage or ignore a zero-gradient failure.
